chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid together, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked him about the owned slave (male or female), how many women are permissible for him to marry? He said: Two free women, or four slave girls. And he said: There is no problem if he has wealth in his possession and is permitted in trade, that he may keep as many concubines as he wishes from the slave girls and have relations with them.

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: Owned slave (male or female), specifically referring to a slave who has been granted partial or full freedom to manage their own affairs.
key_terms.يَتَسَرَّى: To take concubines; to keep female slaves for sexual relations.
key_terms.يَطَأَهُنَّ: To have sexual relations with them.

ai.seo_question: What are the marriage and concubinage rules for an owned slave (mamluk) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific marital and concubinage rights of a 'mamluk' (an owned slave granted autonomy), permitting him to marry two free women or four slave girls, and to keep additional concubines if he possesses financial means and trade permission. It reflects the classical Shia juristic understanding of the mamluk's semi-independent status, distinguishing his rights from both fully free men and other slaves, while emphasizing the economic prerequisites for maintaining a larger household.
